name: courtlistener-1pct
provenance: The file eyecite's benchmark workflow downloads (with no checksum) and runs benchmark/benchmark.py over: a Bernoulli sample of CourtListener opinions published by Free Law Project. id is the CourtListener opinion id; the text columns are as CourtListener stored them. eyecite's .github/workflows/benchmark.yml (v2.7.8) documents the query that made the ten-percent file: COPY (SELECT id, plain_text, html, html_lawbox, html_columbia, html_anon_2020, xml_harvard FROM search_opinion TABLESAMPLE BERNOULLI (0.1)) TO STDOUT WITH (FORMAT csv, ENCODING utf8, HEADER), bzip2-compressed. Postgres reads 0.1 as a percentage, so the one-percent and ten-percent names are labels for the two file sizes, not sampling rates.
